chapter: Names, influences and early blues singers
title: Admired singers: Sophie Tucker and her sister the coon shouter
summary: She went to hear Sophie Tucker at the Palace Theater and admired her sister's shouting and eye-rolling style.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Who were some of the singers that you admired when you were young?

Well, the first singer that I would go every week to see when she was here was Sophie Tucker. She played at the Palace Theater here, and they used to charge 10 cents to go into Pitt. And on Saturdays, I'd hurry up and get my work through, so my mother would let me go up there to listen to her singing. The first song I ever heard her sing was that mesmerizing, meddlesome tune. I've never forgotten it.
Well, what about blues singers? Did you like any blues singers in those days? How did you feel about blues?

Well, I admired my sister, because my sister was, they used to call them, like I told you, coon shouters, you know. And she could shout, and then she used to roll her eyes for one solid chorus. She wouldn't do nothing but just roll, do a whole chorus rolling her eyes, and I went home and went in front of the mirror to see if I could do it. But I never could do it. I never did learn to roll my eyes like my sister, but she could shout, you know. She was a real, what they call a coon shouter.
